chunks.arabic_text: وَسَأَلَ إِسْمَاعِيلُ بْنُ عِيسَى أَبَا الْحَسَنِ الرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ:

translations.en: Isma'il ibn 'Isa asked Abā al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام:

chunks.arabic_text: عَنِ الْجُلُودِ وَالْفِرَاءِ يَشْتَرِيهِ الرَّجُلُ فِي سُوقٍ مِنْ أَسْوَاقِ الْجَبَلِ أَ يَسْأَلُ عَنْ ذَكَاتِهِ إِذَا كَانَ الْبَائِعُ مُسْلِمًا غَيْرَ عَارِفٍ

translations.en: About hides and fur items that a man purchases in a market from the markets of al-Jabal: should he ask about its proper slaughter when the seller is a Muslim but not one possessing recognition?

chunks.arabic_text: قَالَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ «عَلَيْكُمْ أَنْ تَسْأَلُوا عَنْهُ إِذَا رَأَيْتُمُ الْمُشْرِكِينَ يَبِيعُونَ ذَلِكَ وَإِذَا رَأَيْتُمُوهُمْ يُصَلُّونَ فَلَا تَسْأَلُوا عَنْهُ.

translations.en: He عليه السلام said: "You must ask about it if you see the polytheists selling that. But if you see them performing salat, then do not ask about it."

en.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning hides and furs bought in the marketplace and whether one must investigate their proper slaughter. The Imam عليه السلام distinguishes between circumstances that create doubt and those in which the outward sign of Islam, such as performing salat, is treated as sufficient.
en.seo_question: When buying leather or fur from a Muslim seller, must one ask whether it was properly slaughtered?

key_terms.ذَكَاتِهِ: its proper ritual slaughter and purification for lawful use
